preamble: The shift from the bilabial stop [p] to the velar stop [k] moves the closure from the lips to the soft palate; the two places share a low-frequency (grave) acoustic quality. In Northern Sami, Proto-Samic *p became k before a stop or sibilant, as in *vuoptë 'hair' > vuokta and *lëpsē 'dew' > laksi, while the other Sami languages keep p.

examples.note: Northern Sami alone turned *p into k before a stop or sibilant; compare Lule Sami vuoppta, Inari vuopˈtâ.
Compare Lule Sami gippta, Skolt ǩiptt.
Compare Lule Sami sieppte, Inari septi.
Before a sibilant; compare Inari Sami lapse, South Sami lepsie.
